scope.flow: previewWithdraw share calculation in ProgressiveCurve and OffsetProgressiveCurve used by MultiVault withdrawal flow
scope.environment: Solidity vault curve math library (ProgressiveCurve / OffsetProgressiveCurve)

statements.text: A user attempts to withdraw an amount close to totalAssets.
PCMath.square(s) rounds down via standard mul.
previewWithdraw mixes divUp (round up) with square (round down), so the rounded-up deduct can exceed the rounded-down square(s), making sub(PCMath.square(s), deduct) underflow.
previewWithdraw should use consistent rounding directions so that the subtraction of deduct from square(s) does not underflow for withdrawals up to totalAssets.
A withdrawal of all or nearly all assets via previewWithdraw should not revert due to arithmetic underflow.

When a user attempts to withdraw an amount close to `totalAssets`, the rounded-up `deduct` value can exceed the rounded-down `square(s)`, causing `sub(PCMath.square(s), deduct)` to underflow and revert.
Users who attempt to withdraw all or nearly all assets from a vault using `previewWithdraw` can experience unexpected reverts

ambiguities: No explicit attacker or unauthorized-caller condition is stated; the scenario is a user withdrawing near totalAssets.
The report does not give a concrete numeric amount or slope value; the trigger is qualitative (close to totalAssets, small slopes).
Whether the revert is observed in a real transaction or only potential is not established; treated as potential.
MultiVault withdrawal flow being affected is explanatory context, not a distinct stated harm
